questions.stem: The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSPs) are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution (Articles 36–51). Part III contains Fundamental Rights; Part IV-A (added by 42nd Amendment) contains Fundamental Duties.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The concept of Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution was borrowed from which country?
questions.explanation: DPSPs were borrowed from the Irish Constitution of 1937. The Irish in turn had drawn inspiration from the Spanish Constitution.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Directive Principles of State Policy are — in nature, meaning courts cannot enforce them.
questions.explanation: DPSPs are non-justiciable — courts cannot compel the State to implement them. However, they are fundamental to governance and the State must keep them in mind while framing policies.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 44 of the Indian Constitution directs the State to secure for all citizens:
questions.explanation: Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code governing matters such as marriage, divorce, adoption, and inheritance for all citizens across religions.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which article of the Constitution directs the State to provide equal justice and free legal aid to ensure that the legal system is not denied to any citizen by reason of economic disabilities?
questions.explanation: Article 39A (inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976) directs the State to ensure equal justice and free legal aid. This is a Socialistic DPSP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The separation of the judiciary from the executive in public services is directed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 50 directs the State to take steps to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State. This falls under the Liberal-Intellectual DPSPs.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 43A, inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976), deals with:
options: Participation of workers in management of industries
questions.explanation: Article 43A directs the State to take steps to secure the participation of workers in the management of undertakings, establishments, or other organisations engaged in any industry. It was added by the 42nd Amendment.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which article directs the State to promote cottage industries on an individual or co-operative basis in rural areas?
questions.explanation: Article 43 directs the State to secure, by suitable legislation or economic organisation, a living wage and decent standard of life for workers, and to promote cottage industries (Gandhian DPSP).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following DPSPs is classified as Gandhian in nature?
questions.explanation: Article 40 (organisation of village panchayats) is a Gandhian DPSP, reflecting Gandhi's vision of village self-government. Art 44 is Liberal-Intellectual; Art 51 is Liberal-Intellectual; Art 39A is Socialistic.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The original Article 45 directed the State to provide free and compulsory education for all children until they attained which age?
questions.explanation: The original Art 45 set a 10-year timeframe to provide free and compulsory education for children up to 14 years. The 86th Amendment (2002) moved this to Art 21A as a Fundamental Right (6–14 years), while Art 45 now directs early childhood care for children below 6.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which article of the Constitution directs the State to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and other milch and draught cattle?
questions.explanation: Article 48 directs the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and to prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves, and milch and draught cattle. This is a Gandhian DPSP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 47 directs the State to raise the level of nutrition and standard of living and improve public health by prohibiting:
options: Consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs injurious to health
questions.explanation: Article 47 directs the State to regard the raising of nutrition and standard of living as among its primary duties and to prohibit the consumption of intoxicating drinks and drugs harmful to health (a Gandhian DPSP).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Under which sub-clause of Article 39 does the Constitution direct the State to ensure equal pay for equal work for both men and women?
questions.explanation: Article 39(d) directs that there is equal pay for equal work for both men and women. Article 39 as a whole is about securing adequate means of livelihood and preventing concentration of wealth.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 48A, which directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife, was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.explanation: Article 48A was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976. It directs the State to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife of the country.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: DPSPs are covered under which Articles of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: DPSPs span Articles 36 to 51. Article 36 defines the State for Part IV, and Articles 37–51 contain the actual directives. Part III (Fundamental Rights) covers Arts 12–35.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 51 directs the State to endeavour to promote international peace and security and maintain just and honourable relations between nations, and also to foster respect for:
questions.explanation: Article 51 (Liberal-Intellectual DPSP) directs India to foster respect for international law and treaty obligations, encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration, and promote international peace.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: In which landmark Supreme Court case did the Court hold that Parliament cannot give absolute primacy to DPSPs over Fundamental Rights, and that a harmonious balance between the two must be maintained?
questions.explanation: In Minerva Mills Ltd. v. Union of India (1980), the Supreme Court struck down sections of the 42nd Amendment that gave absolute primacy to DPSPs, ruling that the harmony between Fundamental Rights and DPSPs is a basic feature of the Constitution.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 41 directs the State to make effective provision for securing the right to work, to education, and to public assistance in cases of:
options: Unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement
questions.explanation: Article 41 (Socialistic DPSP) directs the State to make effective provision for the right to work, education, and public assistance in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The promotion of educational and economic interests of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and other weaker sections is directed under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 46 (Gandhian DPSP) directs the State to promote with special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections of the people, especially SC and ST, and to protect them from social injustice and exploitation.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about DPSPs is INCORRECT?
options: They are included in Part IV of the Constitution
They were borrowed from the US Constitution
questions.explanation: DPSPs were NOT borrowed from the US Constitution. They were borrowed from the Irish Constitution. The USA's Constitution provided inspiration for Fundamental Rights (like the Bill of Rights), not DPSPs.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Uniform Civil Code envisaged under Article 44 primarily aims at uniformity in which area of law?
questions.explanation: The Uniform Civil Code (Art 44) envisions a common set of civil laws — covering marriage, divorce, adoption, maintenance, and inheritance — applicable to all citizens irrespective of religion.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The provision for 'equal justice and free legal aid' was inserted into the Constitution as Article 39A by which Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: Article 39A was inserted by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, during the Emergency period. It makes free legal aid a directive to the State so that justice is not denied due to economic inability.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which article in Part IV (DPSPs) specifically directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government?
questions.explanation: Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government. This is a Gandhian DPSP.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Article 49 of the Constitution places a duty on the State to protect:
options: Monuments, places and objects of national importance
questions.explanation: Article 49 (Liberal-Intellectual DPSP) directs the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest, declared by Parliament to be of national importance, from spoliation, disfigurement, destruction, removal, disposal, or export.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Directive Principle of State Policy but a Fundamental Right?
options: Right to freedom of speech and expression (Art 19)
questions.explanation: Article 19 (Freedom of Speech and Expression) is a Fundamental Right under Part III, not a DPSP. DPSPs are in Part IV (Arts 36–51); Fundamental Rights are in Part III (Arts 12–35).
questions.subject: Polity
